novelty_flags.label: Theorem 1 consumer
novelty_flags.one_line: “Experimenters can certify optimal weights” gives no named applied domain, paper, or open problem that would use the complete contact-set characterization.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 4, Proposition 4.1 and Theorem 4.2; Appendix B, equations defining W_i and Lemmas S3–S4.
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines the no-interference versus network-linear-in-means problem with g(y)=n^{-1}sum_i beta_{i,3}^2, proves MSE at most C d_max^5/n for its quadratic estimator, and obtains consistency with threshold (d_max^5/n)^{1/4}; Appendix B gives the Bernoulli-half weight and variance ingredients.

Theorem 2 is an asymptotic validity result for an estimated-residual randomization procedure with a corrective factor; the conclusion explicitly lists theoretical power properties as a future direction.

The paper adapts Le Cam mixtures to design-based minimax risk for causal-effect estimation, with a total-variation lower-bound display; it does not state a local testing frontier for the present RMS spillover target.

The paper develops Riesz estimators, unbiasedness/consistency conditions, and conservative variance estimation in a general design-based framework; it does not state the proposed robust conditional-variance game or its least-favourable-prior dual.

The published article studies composite-null testing defined by a quadratic functional in regression and reports minimax separation rates/constants and sharp-optimal tests; this is classical quadratic-testing geometry rather than the fixed-schedule network experiment.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Name a concrete deployment consumer for Theorem 1—such as the LinkedIn-style network experiment of PougetAbadieEtAl2019—and state which motif-level variance decision it changes.

Add a direct comparison corollary quantifying when the optimized motif constant strictly improves GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026's degree-only envelope for a family of nonisomorphic motifs, rather than relying on K3 and C4 alone.
Develop Open-ended Question 7 through the stated orbit-likelihood reduction into a finite limiting experiment, yielding either quadratic optimality or an explicit nonquadratic gain.

recommended_next_step: Revise the Theorem 1 consumer to identify a specific applied use, then advance the field-tier repeated-motif testing-frontier kernel to Stage 0.
